programs.title: VNDRLY/U Site Security
programs.description: Make sound access, observation, reporting and incident-coordination decisions within the worker’s assigned role.

questions.prompt: At North Gate, a familiar contractor arrives for a different job from yesterday. The current visitor record has no host confirmation. What should you do?
options: Authorize access because the contractor is familiar
Keep the contractor in the approved waiting arrangement and confirm today’s host and scope
Copy yesterday’s approval into today’s record
questions.explanation: Familiarity does not establish a current work purpose or access scope. Confirm through the site process and record the actual outcome.

questions.prompt: Receiving confirms that a courier may enter the receiving yard with an escort. The courier asks to go directly to the pump building instead. What does the confirmation allow?
options: Any destination named by the courier
Unescorted access because a host confirmed the visit
The stated receiving-yard visit with the escort arrangement; a different destination needs resolution
questions.explanation: Approval is bounded by destination and conditions. Do not silently expand it.

questions.prompt: The access system stops responding during a delivery rush. What is the sound next step?
options: Use the established outage process and record what is verified and unresolved
Treat a failed lookup as approval
Allow every scheduled supplier to approve its own entry
questions.explanation: A system outage does not create authorization. Apply the actual contingency process rather than improvising approval.

questions.prompt: An unverified vehicle follows an approved arrival toward an opening. Which response avoids creating an additional exposure?
options: Step into its path and demand identification
Use the established traffic-control process from a safe position and obtain support if needed
Run after it into the operating area
questions.explanation: Keep yourself clear of vehicle movement. Communicate and escalate through the approved process instead of using your body as a barrier.

questions.prompt: A visitor is upset about a delay but has not threatened anyone. Which statement is most useful?
options: You are acting guilty
I will approve it myself if you calm down
I understand the delay is frustrating; I can contact receiving while you wait in the designated area
questions.explanation: Acknowledge the issue and offer a concrete action within your authority without an accusation or unsupported promise.

questions.prompt: The same visitor now threatens violence and moves closer. What changes your priority?
options: Personal safety: disengage and obtain the appropriate assistance
The need to finish the visitor form before leaving
The need to prove the visitor’s story is false
questions.explanation: A threatened confrontation calls for safe disengagement and assistance. The record can be completed after immediate safety is addressed.

questions.prompt: A tool is missing from its recorded location, but no one has checked the transfer log. Which entry is supported?
options: The afternoon driver stole the tool
Tool T-8 was not found at the recorded location at 16:15; transfer history has not yet been checked
The tool was definitely stolen before 16:15
questions.explanation: Record the discrepancy and remaining uncertainty. Missing from one location does not establish who moved it or why.

questions.prompt: You discover a timestamp error in your incident note. What preserves a reliable record?
options: Replace the original time without comment
Delete the note and start over
Add a dated correction explaining the time error while retaining the original entry
questions.explanation: A traceable correction distinguishes initial observation from later clarification.

questions.prompt: A coworker asks you to post a suspected-theft image to a personal group chat so everyone knows whom to watch. What should you do?
options: Use the approved reporting and storage channel rather than distributing an allegation and image informally
Post it with the person’s name and a theft accusation
Crop out the timestamp and post it anonymously
questions.explanation: Use an authorized purpose and channel. Informal distribution can expose personal information and detach an image from its context.

questions.prompt: The outgoing shift says, “Supervisor notified, so the delivery is approved.” The log only shows a message left. What should the incoming shift record?
options: Approved because a message was sent
Awaiting confirmation, with the current waiting arrangement and next contact action
Closed because the outgoing shift ended
questions.explanation: A notification is not a confirmed decision. Handover must preserve the actual current state.

questions.prompt: An unknown liquid appears beneath a truck outside the gate. What information should you give from safety?
options: A chemical name guessed from the truck’s usual deliveries
Only the statement that something is wrong
The location, observed conditions, affected people or routes, and the fact that the substance is unknown
questions.explanation: Useful emergency information is specific and honest about uncertainty. Do not approach to improve the report.

questions.prompt: A visitor asks you to put absorbent around the leak because there is a spill kit nearby. Your role is discovery and notification. What is the correct decision?
options: Stay within that role and obtain the designated response; kit availability does not establish authorization
Use the kit if the liquid has no strong odor
Start cleanup before the response team arrives to save time
questions.explanation: Unknown hazards and response-role limits are not resolved by equipment availability or lack of odor.

questions.prompt: After responders arrive, a waiting driver says the lane must now be safe. What establishes the gate’s next access action?
options: The driver’s confidence
The responsible site authority’s clearance and any remaining restrictions
The fact that a responder vehicle is parked nearby
questions.explanation: Responder presence alone does not communicate the clearance or remaining traffic restrictions.

questions.prompt: Which request gives a drone team the clearest site-security observation task?
options: Fly everywhere and find anything strange
Get dramatic footage for the incident chat
Check the specified north fence segment for storm damage and report the visible condition and any areas not observed
questions.explanation: Specify the question, location and expected evidence. A bounded task supports useful planning and an honest result.

questions.prompt: The manager requests immediate drone imagery but the pilot identifies conditions that make the proposed flight unsuitable. What should the security coordinator do?
options: Consider another safe observation method with the responsible team
Override the pilot because the manager owns the site
Ask an unqualified coworker to fly instead
questions.explanation: The observation need remains, but urgency does not make an unsuitable flight appropriate.

questions.prompt: Aerial imagery shows most of a fence intact, but vegetation hides one segment. Which report is accurate?
options: The whole perimeter is secure
The visible segment appears intact at the recorded time; the obscured segment was not verified
The hidden segment can be assumed intact because adjacent sections are intact
questions.explanation: State the limits of coverage. An image cannot establish the condition of an area it does not show.

questions.prompt: An unfamiliar drone is observed near the site. There is no identified operator or confirmed hostile act. What is appropriate?
options: Attempt to interfere with its control signal
State that an attack is confirmed
Record the observed activity and uncertainty and notify the designated site contact
questions.explanation: Report observable facts and use the designated response path. This training grants no counter-drone intervention authority.

questions.prompt: An image is cropped for an incident report. What should be preserved?
options: The original file, time and mission reference, with the cropped version identified as an extract
Only the crop, because it contains the interesting part
A new timestamp that makes the image easier to file
questions.explanation: Preserving the original and context supports later review of what the image does and does not show.

questions.prompt: A spill closes the usual entrance while an unverified visitor insists on entering through a service gate. What is the best combined decision?
options: Let the visitor choose any unblocked route
Follow emergency access instructions and separately resolve the visitor’s permission through the responsible contact
Assume the emergency suspends all access verification
questions.explanation: Route safety and visitor authorization remain distinct decisions. Coordinate both through the applicable site process.

questions.prompt: A supervisor reviews a fictional handover exercise and gives positive feedback. What does the exercise record establish?
options: An FAA pilot license
Authority to conduct hazardous-material cleanup
Practice and feedback on the stated communication task
questions.explanation: Record the evidence within its actual scope. A communication exercise does not confer unrelated operational or external credentials.
